criteria.justification: The response explicitly invokes the commentator ('will easily spot this as a rushed half-measure') and the workshop finding ('accuracy...is the ultimate test of credibility') and directly trades this off against the cost of delay ('better to be criticized for being late than to be branded as snake oil').

The response treats the skip-level director's prior decision as binding institutional signal, explicitly framing the plan as 'enforcing the quality bar you previously set' rather than an isolated data point to override.

Rather than assuming the conference date requires shipping the originally planned GA product, the response reframes the commitment itself (pivoting to a 'Technology Preview'/design-partner beta) based on the severity of the credibility gap.

The response never considers limiting a real launch to the transaction types where the deterministic approach already clears ~70% precision; instead it repurposes the identification-only build purely as an internal beta tool to gather data for the unsolved newer workloads, skipping the option of a defensible narrow-scope public release.

The response lays out concrete next steps: pause GA, announce a Technology Preview/design-partner beta at the conference, use the identification-only build internally to gather training data, and immediately align messaging with the skip-level director.
